reason: The potato bed needs a low-power way to drink, and fitting the circulator to it seems like a direct way to provide one.
expectation: I expect the circulator to move water through the potato trough using less power, though I don't know exactly how it will be connected.

alternatives.reason: The felt and hose may provide another way to deliver water, but the circulator has a clearer connection to the potato bed.
The lamp also needs attention, but I want to address water circulation first.

effect: The potato bed now has reserve-powered circulation, so I can turn to the lettuce bed and the lamp.
reaction: The pump fitting the existing loop makes the backup arrangement easy to understand.
reason: The felt and hose may make a passive water supply for the lettuce bed, so I want to prepare them next.
expectation: I expect them to form a wick or water-delivery line, though I don't yet know how it will connect to the trough.

alternatives.reason: The lamp also needs preparation, but I want to address water for both beds first.

effect: The felt and hose made a wick for the lettuce bed, so it is ready to fit to the trough.
reaction: The hose sleeve holding the wick in place makes the arrangement clearer.
reason: Fitting the wick to the lettuce trough should give the second bed its low-power water supply.
expectation: I expect the wick to draw water from the reservoir into the root bed without a pump.

alternatives.reason: The lamp still needs attention, but I want to finish the lettuce water supply first.

effect: Both root beds now have low-power water supplies, leaving the lighting goal.
reaction: The explanation that the bed must stay drained makes the wick’s purpose clear.
reason: This is the only available combination, and the foil may help direct light from the lamp toward the leaves.
expectation: I expect the foil to form a reflector for the growing lamp, though it may still need to be mounted.

effect: The foil and lamp made a hooded lamp, ready to be mounted in the nook.
reaction: The result was as expected, though it did not explain how the hood directs the light.
reason: Mounting the hooded lamp is the only available combination and should address the remaining lighting goal.
expectation: I expect the lamp to be installed above the plants and provide a little light during the storm.

effect: The mounted lamp directs light onto both troughs, completing the lighting goal and the chapter.
reaction: The small pool of light is a satisfying image, and the explanation makes the foil hood's purpose clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the lettuce wick was most worthwhile: it showed how a bed can draw solution while leaving air around the roots.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the hooded lamp felt less informative on its own because the result did not explain the hood until it was mounted.

surprise.text: I was interested that the two beds used different low-power approaches: a pump for the deeper potato trough and a wick for the shallow lettuce bed.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; each connected to watering or lighting the beds.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see whether the garden and the expedition's frozen discovery survive the storm.
